text:
nina: Quick brain-dump: proposing an "unscoped" API-key mitigation path so we can tighten project scoping without breaking legacy clients. Sharing tradeoffs + a proposed rollout.

aditya: Nice. By "unscoped" do you mean keys that don't map to a project/org in our metadata store?
nina: Exactly. We still see some keys issued early-on or created by older SDKs where we can't reliably recover owner or project. If we immediately require strict project-scoped keys we'll cause outages for those customers.

sam: Core risks: billing attribution, abuse (open endpoints), and support overhead. Also operational complexity if we add a parallel "unscoped" path.

kevin: Security-first constraints: unscoped keys should have a very limited API surface. No admin, no billing edits, and strong rate caps. Internal services must reject them entirely.

nina: Proposed behavior:
1) Any key without project/org gets marked `unscoped=true` and routed to a backstop bucket.
2) Backstop bucket only allowed to call: text-generation (public inference), embeddings (read-only), and health-check endpoints. All write/state endpoints return 403 unless `X-Redwood-Project` present and validated.
3) Require extra headers for exceptions: `X-Redwood-Operator` and `X-Delegation-Proof` for cross-tenant delegation.

aditya: Example allowed request for backstop: 

Authorization: ApiKey sk_unscoped_abc123
X-Redwood-Project: proj_42   # optional, must match delegation proof if present
X-Redwood-Operator: ops@example.com  # optional contact

kevin: About `X-Delegation-Proof` 12 we should require a short-lived signed token for any case where an unscoped key claims a tenant. Prevents silent impersonation.

sam: Migration phases I'd suggest:
- Observe mode (30d): tag calls, emit signals, no behavior change.
- Soft restrict (60d): apply strict rate limits + deny admin endpoints, start notifying owners (where we have contact info).
- Enforce (90d+): reject non-public endpoints and start retiring stale unscoped keys.

nina: On billing: map unscoped usage to a synthetic billing account like `billing:unscoped_region` temporarily so the ledger sees costs. Finance can reassign later.
aditya: Audit/telemetry: emit `api_key.unscoped=true` metric, sample full call logs at 1% for inference but log all denies/quarantines. Add alerts when top unscoped keys contribute >10% traffic.

kevin: Ops note: ops-bot, can we run a staging canary that simulates 10% of production traffic hitting the backstop bucket to check CPU/memory/latency impact?

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary scheduled. Dry-run on staging showed a 2.8x increase in CPU for gpt-type models due to different routing; need to tune batching.

sam: Abuse mitigations: force rotation for any unscoped key seen above threshold QPS, auto-quarantine high-volume keys, and require verified account/email to create new unscoped keys.

nina: UX: Console should surface unscoped keys prominently, include a 1-click 'claim key' flow that maps key to a project and rotates credentials. Also banner in SDK when using an unscoped key (warning + migration link).
aditya: Service-to-service boundary: internal endpoints must only accept mTLS/JWT-presented identities. No unscoped keys for internal RPCs. We should add a guard at the API gateway.

kevin: Edge-case: partner systems that proxy requests and set `X-Redwood-Project` on behalf of clients. We need to validate that the operator or delegation proof matches the project ownership. Otherwise deny.
sam: Logging volume concerns: sample allowed inference calls but always write full logs for policy violations and rejections. Also correlate logs with billing to help reconciliation.

nina: Ownership: I'll draft the RFC for the backstop flow + header semantics + RBAC allow/deny table. @sam can you own abuse/telemetry? @kevin take service validation/mTLS pieces? @aditya help with billing mapping and finance ops?
aditya: Yep, will do billing mapping + finance contacts.

kevin: I'll prototype gateway checks and a unit test matrix for `X-Redwood-Project` + `X-Delegation-Proof` combinations.

ops-bot: [alert] Staging canary shows increased latency for prefix-hits under backstop routing; recommend tuning batching thresholds and KV-cache policy.

nina: Thanks. My next steps: RFC PR with examples, rollout timeline, and a minimal deny-list. Looking to land the doc in 1 week and do a small staging pilot.
aditya: +1 from me.
sam: +1.
kevin: +1.
